issue_context.title: order_by in over is incorrect when grouping column is marked as sorted
issue_context.body:
The first result is correct, the second result should match the first result but it doesn't:

```python
>>> df = pl.DataFrame(
...     {
...         "g": [1, 1, 1, 1],
...         "t": [4, 3, 2, 1],
...         "x": [10, 20, 30, 40],
...     }
... )
...
>>> df.select(pl.col.x.cum_sum().over("g", order_by="t"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌─────┐
│ x   │
│ --- │
│ i64 │
╞═════╡
│ 100 │
│ 90  │
│ 70  │
│ 40  │
└─────┘
>>> df.set_sorted("g").select(pl.col.x.cum_sum().over("g", order_by="t"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌─────┐
│ x   │
│ --- │
│ i64 │
╞═════╡
│ 40  │
│ 70  │
│ 90  │
│ 100 │
└─────┘
```
comments: Running with `POLARS_VERBOSE=1` prints `group_by keys are sorted; running sorted key fast path` only in the second case, so that fast path is likely bugged.

review_comments: `GroupsProxy::Idx` must be explicitly mapped back to the row positions regardless of whether it was sorted

This query internally created a DataFrame of height 5 containing a `list[_]` type column of length 2 (the imploded aggregation result), which it then exploded 🤯 out to the correct height, where the correctness of the result was guaranteed because the DataFrame was sorted beforehand 😂
